text: Sfumato is not blur for its own sake. It is the graduated absence of hard contour so that form emerges from air. Value transitions do the drawing.
On a cheek, seek at least three values rather than a binary light/dark split. The middle value carries the sfumato.
Block the head as planes: forehead, zygomatic, jaw. Expression rides on muscle; muscle rides on bone.
One dominant light creates hierarchy. Equal twin lights flatten conscience. Shadow is not absence — it is volume and judgment.
In a crowd scene, each hand and spine is a sentence. Labor can be shown without caricature when weight and rhythm are observed honestly.
When weather becomes the subject, edges surrender to temperature. Steam, spray, and glare are not effects on top of form — they replace form.
Proportion is a path for the eye, not decoration. Place one focus on a harmonic division, then justify why it earns that place.
